reasons: A clear startup error is given when the build is missing.
The folder check only happens at startup, so a folder removed while running is not reported.

terms.meaning: A common Node.js library for running a web server.
Ready-made files such as pages, images and scripts that are sent to the browser as they are.
A rule that matches any web address not handled by an earlier rule.
The step that turns source code into ready-to-serve files.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for serving web files
sections.what: The top of the file brings in the Express web framework, a file system tool and a path tool. Together they let the server read files from a folder and send them to a visitor's browser.
sections.why: Likely reason: the file is meant to serve built web app files from disk, which needs these tools. Reason not stated in the code beyond the imports.

sections.name: serveStatic
sections.title: Checking the built website folder
sections.what: Starts the setup for serving the website. It finds the public folder and stops with a clear error if the built website is not there.
sections.why: Likely reason: to fail early with a helpful message instead of serving broken pages.
sections.watch_out: The check runs only at startup, so a folder deleted while the server runs is not reported.

sections.name: use
sections.title: Serving the built files
sections.what: Tells the web server to send any matching file from the public folder, such as images, styles or scripts.
sections.why: Likely reason: the browser needs these files to display the site.
sections.watch_out: Anything in the public folder can be downloaded by anyone who can reach the server, so keep private files out of it.

sections.name: use
sections.title: Sending the main page for unknown addresses
sections.what: Any address not matched by an earlier rule gets the main page HTML, so the site's own navigation still works after a refresh.
sections.why: Stated in the code comment: unknown addresses fall through to the main page when the file does not exist.
sections.watch_out: This rule matches everything, so any route added after it is never reached.

summary: When the app runs in production, this serves the built website files and returns the main page for any address the server does not otherwise recognize.
purpose: Lets one server deliver both the data and the web pages, so the owner runs one program instead of two.
why: Likely reason: a single-server setup. The inline comment says unknown addresses fall through to the main page, which lets the in-page navigation work on refresh.
how: Finds the public folder next to the running code. Stops with a clear error if that folder is missing. Tells the web server to serve files from that folder. Adds a final rule that returns the main page for any address not handled earlier.
inputs: The Express web server object passed in by the caller, and the built website files in a folder named public.
outputs: Website files and the main page HTML sent to browsers. A startup error if the built folder is missing.
risks: Routes added after the final catch-all rule will never be reached. The folder is found relative to the running file, so moving the compiled code can break it. The check runs only at startup.
debug: If startup fails with a message about the build directory, run the client build first. If API calls return the main page HTML instead of data, check that the API routes are registered before this function runs. If a file is missing in production, confirm it is inside the public folder.
